answer.approach: Build the smallest end-to-end vertical slice first, then add each milestone behind tests and explicit validation. Keep domain rules independent of HTTP, database, framework, and provider details where practical.
review_checklist: Customer and supplier registration, secure password storage, role checks, and account/session management.
Product categories, product details, variants, inventory, validated image uploads, search, sorting, and pagination.
Cart persistence, server-side price calculation, inventory validation, order lifecycle, and transactional updates.
Payment-provider integration, server-side verification, webhook verification, idempotent payment processing, and failure recovery.
Supplier-specific product and order operations, authorization, inventory updates, and status history.
Shipment creation, address validation, shipping-status synchronization, webhook handling, and retry controls.
Prepared statements, validation, contextual escaping, CSRF protection, resource-level authorization, secure uploads, secret management, and audit logs.
Unit/integration tests, static analysis, Composer, migrations, structured logging, deployment documentation, CI/CD, and rollback planning.
Optional email notifications, background jobs, caching, analytics, refunds, returns, and dispute workflows.
required_evidence: A repeatable setup and test command list.
Tests for normal and failure behavior.
A security review appropriate to the project scope.
A README describing configuration, trade-offs, and limitations.

explanation: This is an architecture and review outline for Clipcart-Style Multi-Vendor E-Commerce Backend; it is not a full production reference implementation. Review all business rules, provider contracts, and security-sensitive details in the actual code.
